The default solver in `CVXR` is `Clarabel`. However, it is not always the
best solver to use. As an example, let us consider again the [catenary
problem](../misc/catenary.qmd).

We will change the problem slightly to use a finer discretization from
101 points to say 501. 


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
## Problem data
m <- 501
L <- 2
h <- L / (m - 1)

## Form objective
x <- Variable(m)
y <- Variable(m)
objective <- Minimize(sum(y))

## Form constraints
constraints <- list(x[1] == 0, y[1] == 1,
                    x[m] == 1, y[m] == 1,
                    diff(x)^2 + diff(y)^2 <= h^2)

## Solve the catenary problem
prob <- Problem(objective, constraints)
result <- psolve(prob, solver = "CLARABEL")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr}

```
Warning: Solution may be inaccurate. Try another solver, adjusting the solver settings,
or solve with `verbose = TRUE` for more information.
```


:::
:::


The solution status is no longer optimal.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
cat("Solution status is", status(prob))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Solution status is optimal_inaccurate
```


:::
:::



::: {.cell}

:::



In such cases, using a different solver may give more accurate
results. Let us try `MOSEK` for example. (MOSEK is a commercial solver; this
section runs only where it is installed.)


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
result <- psolve(prob, solver = "MOSEK")
cat("Solution status is", status(prob))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Solution status is optimal
```


:::
:::



::: {.cell}

:::


This returns an optimal solution. 

Different solvers have varying strengths, and it is worth trying
alternatives when one solver does not produce satisfactory results.
